page: Amazon Web Services r8i.2xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and int8 operations. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2111.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 34.01 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Text processing performance is highly competitive, reaching 2958.0 in Geekbench, which ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall within the average range, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 8639.03 and an uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 76.86 GB/sec. Redis SET operations average 15.16 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reaches 16.02 GB/sec.

The instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high baseline network speeds, as network bandwidth is limited to 4 Gbps. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage options. Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the r8i.2xlarge is suitable for database operations, memory-intensive text processing, software compilation, and small-to-medium scale LLM inference tasks.
